summary: Task 1 is a three-line graph of museum visitors over 15 years and Task 2 an agree/disagree essay about investing in young people; both are phrased the IELTS way. The only problem is that one of the three "types of visitor" in the graph is not a type of visitor.
strengths: Task 1 has clear contrasting trends (adults up then slightly down, children falling, special exhibitions small but rising) that reward comparison.
Task 2 is a genuine IELTS-style opinion prompt with the standard instruction and rubric.

issues.problem: The prompt says "three types of visitors", but the third line in writing/day2.svg is labelled "Special exhibitions", which is an attraction, not a type of visitor. Careful candidates will be unsure what that line counts.
issues.change: Relabel the legend "Visitors to special exhibitions" in day2.svg, or change the prompt to "the number of visits to a museum by adults and by children under 15, and visits to its special exhibitions, between 1997 and 2012".
